short: Military allotment system that provided Sweden with a highly trained standing army.
full:
Formalized by parliamentary decision on 27 October 1682 under Charles XI, the Late Allotment System (Yngre indelningsverket) radically reorganized the Swedish military. Instead of unreliable conscription, groups of farmers (rotes) were required to provide and support a professional soldier with a cottage and a plot of land.

This localized support network gave Sweden a well-trained, permanently standing army and navy that could be mobilized rapidly without bankrupting the state. The system successfully sustained the empire's military capabilities through the Great Northern War and remained the foundation of Swedish defense until the early twentieth century.
